I am considering [[locally graded categories]] but I won't write "locally". I won't bother with size issues.
Let G\mathbb{G}G be a symmetric monoidal category, GCat\mathbb{G}\mathbf{Cat}GCat be the category of G\mathbb{G}G-graded categories, and Cat\mathbf{Cat}Cat be the category of categories. I have three constructions to "erase grades" in a graded category and I am looking for how to name them or references to similar constructions.

Let C\mathbf{C}C be a G\mathbb{G}G-graded category. We have three categories with the same objects as C\mathbf{C}C, and corresponding functors F1,F2,F3:GCat→CatF_1,F_2,F_3: \mathbb{G}\mathbf{Cat} \rightarrow \mathbf{Cat}F1​,F2​,F3​:GCat→Cat.

  1. If III is the unit of the monoidal structure on G\mathbb{G}G, there is a category CI\mathbf{C}_ICI​ of III-graded morphisms (because I⊗I=II \otimes I = II⊗I=I, so composition and tensor remains in CI\mathbf{C}_ICI​.)
  2. There is also a category C∪\mathbf{C}_{\cup}C∪​ whose morphisms are all the graded morphisms of C\mathbf{C}C (but their grades are forgotten), i.e. C∪(X,Y)=⋃γ∈Ob(G)Cγ(X,Y)\mathbf{C}_{\cup}(X,Y) = \bigcup_{\gamma \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathbb{G})} \mathbf{C}_{\gamma}(X,Y)C∪​(X,Y)=⋃γ∈Ob(G)​Cγ​(X,Y).
  3. If we denote ∼\sim∼ to be the least congruence on morphisms in C\mathbf{C}C containing (f,g)(f,g)(f,g) whenever f=t⋆gf = t \star gf=t⋆g for some morphism t∈Gt \in \mathbb{G}t∈G (in words, fff and ggg are equal up to regrading), then there is a category C∪/∼\mathbf{C}_{\cup}/{\sim}C∪​/∼ where morphisms are equivalence classes of graded morphisms.

We can also go the other way H1,H2:Cat→GCatH_1,H_2 : \mathbf{Cat} \rightarrow \mathbb{G}\mathbf{Cat}H1​,H2​:Cat→GCat where any category D\mathbf{D}D can become a G\mathbb{G}G-graded category in two ways:

  1. You make a graded category where all morphisms of D\mathbf{D}D have grade III.
  2. You make a graded category where all morphisms of D\mathbf{D}D have all possible grades of G\mathbb{G}G, so there are multiple graded morphism for each morphism in D\mathbf{D}D.

We also have some relations between these functors like F1∘H1=F1∘H2=idF_1 \circ H_1 = F_1 \circ H_2 = \mathrm{id}F1​∘H1​=F1​∘H2​=id. I am also pretty sure that F3⊣H2⊣F1F_3 \dashv H_2 \dashv F_1F3​⊣H2​⊣F1​.

I call the result of F1F_1F1​ the 'underlying category' following Definition 8.1 here and Definition 12 here. But I don't think I have seen either of the other definitions.

This isn't an answer to your question, but am I correct in understanding that these functors are all arising from change-of-base functors between Set and [G^op, Set]? If so, perhaps these can be used to determine suitable names the constructions?
(2) isn't well defined unless G\mathbb GG is strict, and therefore doesn't seem a natural construction (even though it may seem reasonable at first glance).

Good point about (2) and strictness. I was indeed implicitly assuming G\mathbb{G}G is strict, but I did not realize it was important here.

To be explicit: associativity and unitality of the composition in the category would fail because, e.g. for associativity, h∘(g∘f)h \circ (g \circ f)h∘(g∘f) would not be the same morphism as (h∘g)∘f(h \circ g) \circ f(h∘g)∘f because they don't have the same grade (the grades are equal up to an associator), so they would be part of a different term of the disjoint union in C(X,Y)\mathbf{C}(X,Y)C(X,Y).

Thanks.

I still don't have a good grasp of the enriched point of view for graded categories, mostly because of Day convolution. (I've been working on graded categories for 2 years...) Tell me if I am making sense.

  1. There is a functor evaluating presheaves at III: −(I):[Gop,Set]→Set-(I) : [\mathbb{G}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathbf{Set}] \rightarrow \mathbf{Set}−(I):[Gop,Set]→Set sends PPP to P(I)P(I)P(I). It's clearly monoidal. Change of base along this functor should be equivalent to F1F_1F1​.
  2. There is also a functor taking the disjoint union of all evaluations: ∪:[Gop,Set]→Set\cup : [\mathbb{G}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathbf{Set}] \rightarrow \mathbf{Set}∪:[Gop,Set]→Set sends PPP to ∪γ∈GP(γ)\cup_{\gamma \in \mathbb{G}} P(\gamma)∪γ∈G​P(γ). It's less clearly monoidal. I guess checking that will involve strictness of G\mathbb{G}G, otherwise my previous answer would be invalidated. Change of base along this functor should be equivalent to F2F_2F2​.
  3. For F3F_3F3​, since we are taking a quotient of a disjoint union, I am guessing it will be some kind of colimit. Indeed, colim:[Gop,Set]→Set\mathrm{colim} :[\mathbb{G}^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathbf{Set}] \rightarrow \mathbf{Set}colim:[Gop,Set]→Set is a functor. I don't know if it is monoidal. It's left adjoint, so it preserves colimits. Day convolution is a kind of colimit. So that's encouraging. I don't have a clear intuition that this colimit will correspond to the quotient by the congruence generated by "up to regrading". But it does not sound too far either.

Have these change of base functors been named before ?
Sorry to be dense, but what's a G\mathbb{G}G-graded category for a symmetric monoidal category G\mathbb{G}G?

It's what some people call [[locally graded category]], the quickest definition is that it is a [Gop,Set][\mathbb{G}^\mathrm{op},\mathbf{Set}][Gop,Set]-enriched category, where the base of enrichment is equipped with Day convolution as a monoidal product. The symmetry in G\mathbb{G}G is not required to define this.
So for a category where the homsets are Z\mathbb{Z}Z-graded I take G\mathbb{G}G to be the discrete monoidal category where the objects are elements of the monoid Z\mathbb{Z}Z, I guess?

Have these change of base functors been named before ?

I don't know where these constructions are explicitly mentioned anywhere, but they are most naturally seen from the perspective of graded categories as local discrete fibrations (over the delooping of G\mathbb GG). For this correspondence, see Theorem 9.6 and Corollary 10.9 of Exponentiable virtual double categories and presheaves for double categories, for instance.

Every G\mathbb GG-graded category induces a local discrete fibration over the delooping of G\mathbb GG, and thus is equipped with the structure of a bicategory (namely, the source of the local discrete fibration). When G\mathbb GG is strict, this bicategory is a 2-category, and its underlying category is the one you describe.

The third construction is given by taking the quotient of this 2-category by the relation induced by the 2-cells.

Hi Ralph. I do think your description of (3) in terms of change of base along colim\mathrm{colim}colim is correct, and the description in terms of the least congruence comes directly from the concrete description of colimits in Set.

Let M\mathcal{M}M be a [Gop,Set][\mathbb{G}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathbf{Set}][Gop,Set]-enriched category. That is, for every pair of objects, we have a presheaf M(A,B):Gop→Set\mathcal{M}(A,B) : \mathbb{G}^\mathrm{op} \to \mathbf{Set}M(A,B):Gop→Set, and so for every triple of a pair of objects and a grade (object of G\mathbb{G}G), we have a set Mg(A;B):=M(A;B)(g)\mathcal{M}_g(A;B) := \mathcal{M}(A;B)(g)Mg​(A;B):=M(A;B)(g) and for every morphism g′→gg' \to gg′→g in G\mathbb{G}G we have a function Mg(A;B)→Mg′(A;B)\mathcal{M}_g(A;B) \to \mathcal{M}_{g'}(A;B)Mg​(A;B)→Mg′​(A;B) (regrading).

If we change base along colim\mathrm{colim}colim, our hom-object becomes colim(M(A;B))\mathrm{colim}(\mathcal{M}(A;B))colim(M(A;B)), which concretely is ∐g∈GMg(A;B)\coprod_{g \in G} \mathcal{M}_g(A;B)∐g∈G​Mg​(A;B) quotiented by ... (exactly as in your original post).

To see that colim\mathrm{colim}colim is monoidal, you can use abstract nonsense in the monoidal equipment Prof as follows. Let P,Q:1↛GP,Q : 1 \nrightarrow GP,Q:1↛G be presheaves. Convolution is the composite (F×G)⊙⊗∗(F \times G) \odot \otimes_{*}(F×G)⊙⊗∗​, and colimit is composition with !∗:G↛1!_{*} : G \nrightarrow 1!∗​:G↛1. Then we have

(F×G)⊙⊗∗⊙!∗≅(F×G)⊙(!∘⊗)∗≅(F×G)⊙(!×!)∗≅(F×G)⊙(!∗×!∗)≅(F⊙!∗)×(G⊙!∗)(F \times G) \odot \otimes_{*} \odot !_{*} \cong (F \times G) \odot {(! \circ \otimes)}_* \cong (F \times G) \odot {(! \times !)}_* \cong (F \times G) \odot (!_* \times !_*) \cong (F \odot !_*) \times (G \odot !_*)(F×G)⊙⊗∗​⊙!∗​≅(F×G)⊙(!∘⊗)∗​≅(F×G)⊙(!×!)∗​≅(F×G)⊙(!∗​×!∗​)≅(F⊙!∗​)×(G⊙!∗​)

(via companions preserve composition, Cat is cartesian monoidal, companions preserve monoidal structure, interchange in monoidal double category). For a reference, Im-Kelly I think contains all the bits (in 5.1, take A=G,C=SetA = G, C=\mathsf{Set}A=G,C=Set and push the terminal presheaf right-to-left along the equivalence).

(By the way, we did consider a version of (2) and (3) in our MFPS paper (Propositions 5.1 and 5.6).)
Amazing! Thanks. I'll definitely add your variant to my references.
